draft.title: Characteristics of an effective law
card: An effective law is one that people follow and that does its job. Five characteristics are used to judge this.
the law matches what most people in society believe is right. People are more willing to obey a law they agree with.
the law can be put into practice. Police and courts must be able to detect breaches and apply a penalty.
people can find out about the law, and its wording is easy to understand. A person cannot follow a rule they have never heard of or cannot make sense of.
the law does not change too often, so people can plan around it. It can still change over time when society changes.
draft.remember: An effective law matches values, can be enforced, is known, is clear and is stable.

a.q: A new law is written in such complicated wording that most people cannot tell what it requires. Which characteristic is it missing?
a.why: Clear means the wording can be understood. People cannot follow a rule they cannot make sense of. Stability is about how often a law changes, not how it is worded.
a.clue: Think about the wording, not how often the law changes.

b.q: A council bans dogs from a beach, but has no rangers and no way to check who brings a dog. Most locals support the ban. Which characteristic is the law weakest on?
b.why: Without rangers or any way to detect breaches, the council cannot apply a penalty, so the law is hard to enforce. It does reflect values, because most locals support it, so that is not its weakness.
b.clue: Most locals agree with the ban, so look at what happens after someone breaks it.

proposal.title: Characteristics of an effective law
card: An effective law is one that people follow and that does its job. It has five characteristics: it reflects society's values, and it is enforceable, known, clear and stable.
Reflecting values means the law matches what most people believe is right, so they are more willing to obey it. Enforceable means police and courts can detect breaches and apply a penalty.
Known means people can find out about the law. Clear means its wording is easy to understand, so people can tell what it requires.
Stable means the law does not change too often, so people can plan around it. It can still change over time when society changes.
proposal.remember: People are more likely to follow a law they agree with, know about, understand, can be caught breaking and can rely on.

a.q: A new law is written in such complicated wording that most people cannot tell what it requires. Which characteristic is it missing?
a.why: Clear means the wording can be understood, so people can tell what the law requires. Stability is about how often a law changes, not how it is worded.
a.clue: Think about the wording, not how often the law changes.

b.q: A council has banned dogs from a beach for ten years. Signs at each entrance explain the ban and most locals support it, but there are no rangers and no way to check who brings a dog. Which characteristic is the law weakest on?
b.why: Without rangers or any way to detect breaches, the council cannot apply a penalty, so the law is hard to enforce. It does reflect values, because most locals support it, and the signs mean it is known.
b.clue: Most locals agree with the ban, so look at what happens after someone breaks it.
